title: Trump Administration Considers Putting Nuclear Power Plants in US Waters
source_used: Bloomberg text as carried by Energy Connects (22 Jul 2026)
key_facts: The Trump administration is exploring nuclear power projects in the 3.2 billion acres of federal waters managed by the US government.

An agreement announced Wednesday between the Interior Department's Marine Minerals Administration and the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission aims to strengthen cooperation in evaluating undersea nuclear power plants.
No commercial nuclear power plants are approved or planned in federal waters; the agreement is to assess whether and how the technology could be 'responsibly implemented'.
Matt Giacona, the Marine Minerals Administration's acting director, said submerged reactor systems have been deployed safely in naval applications for decades.
The same day the Department of Transportation and the Port of Long Beach signed a memorandum of cooperation to test small modular reactors for commercial vessels and other uses.
quote_evidence: No commercial nuclear power plants are approved or planned in federal waters, but the agreement is designed to assess whether and how the technology could be “responsibly implemented” in the future, the Marine Minerals Administration said.
The Trump administration is exploring the potential for nuclear power projects in the 3.2 billion acres of federal waters managed by the US government.
why_it_matters_hint: Only a study agreement; no plant is approved or planned.
